neighbours.label: plant photosynthesis / chloroplast biochemistry context (chloroplast, thylakoid, stroma, chlorophyll, stomata, plant hormones)
fire: Inside the leaf, carbon fixation takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.
Light striking photosystem I drives electrons through ferredoxin to NADP reductase.
Guard cells swell with water and open the stomata when light levels rise.
The thylakoid lumen becomes acidic as protons are pumped across the membrane.
Under stress, plants accumulate jasmonic acid, which activates defence genes in the leaves.
Chlorophyll b absorbs blue light and passes the energy to the reaction centre.
The enzyme Rubisco sometimes binds oxygen, which leads to photorespiration in the leaf.
Etioplasts turn into chloroplasts within hours once the seedling is exposed to light.
quiet: Inside the muscle, glucose breakdown takes place in the cytoplasm of the cell.
Oxygen entering the lungs binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells.
Kidney cells take up water and salts when hormone levels in the blood rise.
The stomach lining becomes acidic as protons are pumped by parietal cells.
Under stress, the body releases cortisol, which raises blood sugar levels.
Melanin absorbs ultraviolet light and protects the skin from sunburn.
The gardener sprinkled compost around the tomatoes and tied them to stakes.
Insulin is released by the pancreas soon after a meal rich in sugar.
